_comment: STAGED, apply_ready=false — the G4 asymmetric-presence completion of ffs0#174 item 3. Adds the two seat agents the t263 membership batch DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED because they had no node on the Z440 fold (see t263-membership-topology.staged.json staging_notes: 'vscode.hp-laptop.copilot + vscode.hpprodesk.primary — NOT nodes in the Z440 fold — LINK would ErrNodeNotFound; ride the laptop/ProDesk replication round'). This IS that round. Membership is a FLEET register that lives on the Z440 fold (ffs0#174 ruling: 3 of the 8 t263 members are laptop-resident, so the register is not per-fold) — so these nodes + links belong on hp-z440.primary, NOT on the ProDesk/laptop folds. Because both agents 404 on the Z440 fold today, each is ADD-then-LINK, not a bare LINK. OPERATOR SAFETY: Test-MoosFederation.ps1 -Mode PostProgram reads ONLY the .envelopes array and does NOT honor apply_ready/applied/review_only — do NOT run it on this file until you have flipped apply_ready and checked the readback gate by hand.
staging_notes: HARD GATE: /healthz must show ontology_version 4.0.4 first — member-of (WF02) is undeclared below 4.0.4 and every LINK would reject. Z440 primary is 4.0.4 as of T=264.

SHAPE: each agent is ADD (node) -> LINK WF02 member-of (group:moos). The ADD is REQUIRED: both agents return HTTP 404 on /state/nodes today, so a bare member-of LINK ErrNodeNotFound's. This is exactly why t263 excluded them.

MEMBERSHIP ONLY, no WF01 owns — verified against the live fold: group:sam owns 0 agents (its 9 owns targets are 3 kernels, 3 sessions, 2 purposes, 1 program), and none of the 8 t263 sibling agents carry an inbound owned-by. The register's actual pattern is member-of without owns; adding an owns LINK here would make these two the ONLY WF01-owned agents in the fold — a misleading 2-node ownership island. So this batch matches the sibling pattern exactly: node + member-of. (An earlier draft included owns 'for completeness' on a false premise; struck after live check.)
ACTOR: kernel:hp-z440.primary throughout, matching the t263 membership batch this extends (kernel actor bypasses M11/M12; required for ontology-governed ADDs and WF02 authority LINKs).
SCOPE: Z440 primary fold ONLY (R1 sovereignty). Does NOT touch the ProDesk or laptop folds. ProDesk must NOT ADD group:moos locally (ffs0#174 ruling).

PROPERTY SCOPES match the 4.0.4 agent operad, which declares transport_type / invocation_protocol / model / board_id / status as authority_scope:'kernel' (these mutable props are kernel-authority, §M12). Note this is DESCRIPTIVE: ValidateADD ignores the supplied authority_scope and ValidateMUTATE reads the operad registry, not the stored property — so the stored value never gates. Set to 'kernel' anyway so the persisted metadata agrees with the operad rather than the legacy 'owner' the older sibling nodes happen to store.

created_at values are placeholders (t264 wall date). The OPERATOR applying this should stamp the real apply-time UTC or leave the kernel to default — Test-MoosFederation does not stamp; it POSTs bytes verbatim.
Revocation of any membership = UNLINK on the relation_urn; window per the accepted t263 doctrine sentence.

APPLY: flip apply_ready -> true, then Test-MoosFederation.ps1 -Mode PostProgram -Persona zappa against live :8000 on 4.0.4. Expected: 4/4 (2 ADD, 2 WF02); /state/relations then shows 13 member-of. (Baseline moved 10 -> 11 at T=266 when the t266-lp-wiring batch LINKed group:moos member-of group:my-tiny-data-collider, log 644-668; expect_after updated accordingly — coordination bus ffs0#178.)

t274 (Sam, rev-4): vscode-codex.hp-z440 bundled per ruling — agent node verified live on hp-z440.primary; register expectation 13 -> 14. apply_ready flipped t274; pre-bump apply per Guido correction 2 (readback_gate stays 4.0.4).
